name: Non-HTTP probe adapters
purpose: Owns the non-HTTP transports the shipped profile set names: `dockerHealthcheck` (exec-transport, an entry-point command whose exit code is the probe answer), `systemd` (supervisor-notify transport, an `sd_notify(READY=1)` at boot followed by periodic `WATCHDOG=1` calls at the operator-configured cadence), and TCP-socket transport (a listener that completes the TCP handshake on pass and refuses the connection on fail, used by the Kubernetes `TCPSocket` probe mode when the operator selects it). No HTTP listener is opened for a process running only a non-HTTP profile.
responsibilities: For the `dockerHealthcheck` profile, expose an entry-point command whose invocation reads the readiness predicate and exits with code 0 on pass and a non-zero code on fail; the process itself opens no HTTP probe listener (AC-14105-3).

For the `systemd` profile with `Type=notify`, call `sd_notify(READY=1)` exactly once after the process reaches its ready state at boot; when a watchdog cadence is declared, call `sd_notify(WATCHDOG=1)` at that cadence for the process lifetime.

For a Kubernetes profile whose `transport` override is `tcpSocket`, open a TCP listener on the resolved probe port; on pass, accept the connection and close it cleanly; on fail, close the accept socket so the kubelet's connect attempt is refused.
Ensure a non-HTTP profile's adapter selection is exclusive: the process does not open a probe HTTP listener when the selected profile's transport is `exec`, `notify`, or `tcpSocket` (AC-14105-3).
internalStructure: Three sibling submodules gated by the profile's `transport` value: `execAdapter` exposes a `runHealthcheck({ readinessPredicate })` function suitable for a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK CMD`; `notifyAdapter` exposes `announceReady()` and `startWatchdog({ cadenceMs })` helpers wrapping the operator-supplied notify implementation; `tcpAdapter` exposes `openTcpProbeListener({ port, readinessPredicate })`. The profile resolver's `transport` value selects exactly one adapter per boot; the rest stay dormant.

interfaces.name: selectAdapter
interfaces.description: selectAdapter({ profile, readinessPredicate, notifyImplementation, tcpFactory }) -> { adapter }. Returns the correct adapter object for the profile's transport. `notifyImplementation` is a project-supplied `(msg: string) -> void` wrapping the supervisor notify call for the runtime (systemd's `NOTIFY_SOCKET` on Linux, a stub in tests). `tcpFactory` is a project-supplied `(port) -> TcpListener`. Called once at boot when the profile transport is non-HTTP.

interfaces.name: notifyImplementation
interfaces.description: Project-supplied notify writer accepting a supervisor-format message string. For systemd, this writes to the `NOTIFY_SOCKET` datagram address. For tests, a stub accumulator. Injected so the blueprint holds no operating-system-specific dependency.

dependencies.name: profile resolver
dependencies.description: Selects which non-HTTP adapter to instantiate from the frozen profile's transport value.

tradeoffs: The non-HTTP transports the blueprint supports out of the box are the three that appear most on the supervisor conventions the shipped profile set targets. Other supervisor transports (gRPC health, a custom binary protocol) belong to a project-authored `custom:<name>` profile that supplies its own adapter through the same selection surface; the blueprint declines to ship every possible non-HTTP transport because the maintenance cost outstrips the value at the rcf-lite tier this blueprint targets. The alternative (a universal transport-abstraction interface) leaks its shape into every profile and every consumer without a real payoff for the three transports actually shipped.
